13005.text: Power: The ruler's anger is followed at once by a command: custody, a decree, destruction, killing. "A king's wrath is like the growling of a lion".

13036.text: A person's anger leads to a command, where the angry one has power: "and he put them in custody"; "commanded that all the wise men of Babylon be destroyed"; Herod "sent and killed all the male children in Bethlehem".

13089.text: The anger that imprisons also places: "But the Lord was with Joseph" (Joseph in prison after Potiphar's anger; the officers Pharaoh imprisoned in anger later bring about his release, Gen 41:9–13).

13142.text: Sequence in Isa 63:1–64:12: no one to help → God's arm alone → "I will recount the steadfast love" → "you were angry, and we sinned" → no one who calls → "we are the clay … please look".

13540.text: Power (new): the ruler's anger becomes a command at once: Verses: Gen 40:2–3; Dan 2:12; Est 1:12–19.

13579.text: angry → put them in custody (Gen 40:2–3); refused to come → enraged → counsel → decree (Est 1:12–19); angry → commanded the wise men destroyed → they sought Daniel (Dan 2:12–13); provokes him → forfeits his life (Pro 20:2).

13752.text: God hardens a human seat (19 verses): Pharaoh (Exo 4:21; 7:3; 9:12; 10:1, 20, 27; 11:10; 14:4, 8) and the Egyptians (14:17); Sihon, "the Lord your God hardened his spirit and made his heart obstinate" (Deu 2:30); the Canaanites (Jos 11:20); "Make the heart of this people dull [heavy]" (Isa 6:10); "why do you ... harden our heart?" (Isa 63:17); Joh 12:40; Rom 9:18; "I gave them over to their stubborn hearts" (Psa 81:12).

13758.text: God's own seat in delight and aversion, none of it hardened: "my soul delights" (Isa 42:1; Mat 12:18); "his soul hates the wicked" (Psa 11:5); "an abomination to his soul" (Pro 6:16); "my soul hates ... I am weary of bearing them" (Isa 1:14); "I abhor the pride of Jacob" (Amo 6:8, sworn "by himself"); "my soul has no pleasure in him" (Heb 10:38); "my soul will abhor you" (Lev 26:30; negated in 26:11); "the beloved of my soul" handed over (Jer 12:7); the human question "Does your soul loathe Zion?" (Jer 14:19).

13997.text: In Joseph's story the anger that imprisons also positions. "The Lord was with Joseph" in the prison (Gen 39:21), and the officers imprisoned by Pharaoh's anger bring about Joseph's release (41:9–13).

14198.text: What it does to the one who holds it. It turns at once into custody or death: Potiphar, hearing his wife's story, "his anger was kindled", and "Joseph's master took him and put him into the prison" (Gen 39:19–20); "Pharaoh was angry with his two officers … and he put them in custody" (Gen 40:2–3; recalled at 41:10); the king "arose in his wrath" and says "Hang him on that" (Est 7:7, 10).

14199.text: What it does to those beneath it: Pleading against it before it rises:; Judah: "let not your anger burn against your servant, for you are like Pharaoh himself" (Gen 44:18). The plea is a long retelling of the father's love (44:19–21 onward); Rachel: "Let not my lord be angry that I cannot rise before you, for the way of women is upon me" (Gen 31:35). The plea for no anger covers a concealment: she is sitting on the stolen gods (31:34); Reading it as a sign: "If he says, 'Good!' it will be well with your servant, but if he is angry, then know that harm is determined by him" (1Sa 20:7). Saul's anger is to be read as the evidence of Saul's intent. Jonathan's knowledge follows the same path: after the spear, "Jonathan knew that his father was determined to put David to death" (20:33); Anticipating it and scripting a reply: Joab to the messenger: "if the king's anger rises, and if he says to you, 'Why did you go so near the city?' … then you shall say, 'Your servant Uriah the Hittite is dead also'" (2Sa 11:20–21). The anger is foreseen, and so is the one sentence that will turn it. That sentence works because the king had wanted Uriah dead. The line manages the king's anger by exposing the king's own secret; Plotting against it from below: "Bigthan and Teresh … became angry and sought to lay hands on King Ahasuerus" (Est 2:21). This is anger rising from the servants, discovered through Mordecai (2:22); Anger acting covertly: Zebul, "when [he] heard the words of Gaal … his anger was kindled. And he sent messengers to Abimelech secretly" (Judg 9:30–31). Anger turned into an ambush plan, "set an ambush in the field" (9:32); A group overrules its king: "the commanders of the Philistines were angry with him … 'Send the man back … how could this fellow reconcile himself to his lord?'" (1Sa 29:4). The king Achish yields: "Nevertheless, the lords do not approve of you" (29:6). The anger comes from suspicion: they fear a loyalty they cannot see.

14202.text: What it leads to. Imprisonment (Joseph, the officers), hanging (the baker, Haman, the eunuchs), a friend sent away (David from the Philistines): In Joseph's story the anger that imprisons also positions. "The Lord was with Joseph" in the prison (Gen 39:21), and the officers imprisoned by Pharaoh's anger bring about Joseph's release (41:9–13).

14494.text: What it does. Two different occasions: At the call: "Oh, my Lord, please send someone else." "Then the anger of the Lord was kindled against Moses" (Exo 4:13–14). The anger is answered at once by provision: Aaron "is coming out to meet you, and when he sees you, he will be glad in his heart" (4:14); "I will be with your mouth and with his mouth" (4:15); At the end: "Even with me the Lord was angry on your account and said, 'You also shall not go in there'" (Deu 1:37); "the Lord was angry with me because of you and would not listen to me … 'Enough from you; do not speak to me of this matter again'" (3:26); "I must die in this land; I must not go over the Jordan" (4:21–22).

14682.text: How it co-exists: No one left to help: "There is none to guide her among all the sons she has borne" (Isa 51:18); "who will console you? … who will comfort you?" (51:19); "drunk, but not with wine" (51:21); Humiliation: "you have made your back like the ground and like the street for them to pass over" (51:23); The community lament uses the same image: "you have given us wine to drink that made us stagger".

14683.text: What it leads to. The cup is taken away and given to the tormentors: "Behold, I have taken from your hand the cup of staggering; the bowl of my wrath you shall drink no more; and I will put it into the hand of your tormentors" (Isa 51:22–23). It is done by "your God who pleads the cause of his people" (51:22).

14684.text: Seat. None in-verse. Outside: Isa 51:23 "to you" (nephesh). Zion's self. Self-sense. Not found in the batches.

14685.text: Revisit of U1 §34 and its pointer. U1 §34 is "anger and passion as a drink given to others" (Hab 2:15; Rev 14:8; 18:3). Its pointer was "the cup that comes round" (Hab 2:16; Rev 14:10): Isa 51:22–23 is the cup coming round: taken from the one who drank and given to the tormentors; Part C (Hab 2:16; Rev 14:10) will be read against it.

14749.text: Where it comes from: Refused cleansing: "because I would have cleansed you and you were not cleansed from your uncleanness, you shall not be cleansed anymore till I have satisfied my fury upon you" (24:13); Effort without change: "She has wearied herself with toil; its abundant corrosion does not go out of it" (24:12); Blood left uncovered (24:7).

14829.text: (v2) Isa 51:17–23: Sequence the text gives: cup drunk to the dregs → "There is none to guide her" → sons fainted, "full of the wrath" → cup taken, given to the tormentors; Phenomena: CP.

14831.text: (v2) Isa 63:1–64:12: Sequence the text gives: no one to help → God's arm alone → "I will recount the steadfast love" → "you were angry, and we sinned" → no one who calls → "we are the clay … please look"; Phenomena: NI · CL.

14836.text: (v3) Eze 9:1–10: Sequence the text gives: abominations → mark on those who sigh and groan → slaughter begins at the sanctuary → the prophet alone, face down: "Will you destroy all the remnant?" → "my eye will not spare"; Phenomena: IN.

14924.text: (v2) Isa 51:22 (CP): Context seat: Isa 51:23 "said to you" nephesh; Whose · check: Zion's self · self-sense; Already read in: — (not found in the batches); §: §40.

15724.text: H7379 (riv) is a distinct, formal legal and covenant-lawsuit term, not domestic quarrelling: case at law, dispute in court, and repeatedly God's own formal indictment against Israel or the nations (Mic 6:2, the LORD has an indictment against his people; Jer 25:31; Isa 41:21). This is forensic vocabulary, structurally closer to family D (crime and injustice) than to the Proverbs strife nouns it was grouped with.

15880.text: Revisit 2026-09-28: Pharaoh's hardening is also expressed by *ḥāzaq* "make strong" (Exo 4:21; 7:13; 14:4, 8), which is filed in M23 Strength & Courage. The same verb gives "be strong, let your heart take courage" (Psa 27:14).; In context (Exo 14:4–8), the hardening gives firmness to a change of heart Pharaoh had already made ("What is this we have done?", 14:5).; See Batch G §3.3. The data therefore hold hardening under grief (heavy), rebellion (Batch C §9.3) and strength, according to the root.

15932.text: Wonders set against a hardened heart: "I will harden Pharaoh's heart, and though I multiply my signs and wonders" (Exo 7:3; 4:21; 11:10).

15963.text: 1.10 Heart and mind (nous / dianoia) side by side: "put my laws into their minds, and write them on their hearts" / "on their hearts … on their minds" (Heb 8:10 / 10:16); "guard your hearts and your minds" (Phili 4:7); The love command lists heart, soul, mind and strength as separate items (Mar 12:30; Mat 22:37; Luk 10:27); Revisit 2026-09-28 (context Mar 12:28–34, Batch F §2): the scribe repeats the command as "heart … understanding [*synesis*] … strength" (12:33). He replaces soul with a knowing word, and Jesus calls the answer wise (12:34). The faculty list is not fixed; what stays constant is "all".; "evil thoughts [reasonings]" come "out of the heart" (Mat 15:19; Mar 7:21); "the reasoning of their hearts" (Luk 9:47)

15966.text: 2.1 "Wise of heart" = skilled ◆: "every skillful craftsman" = *wise of heart* (Exo 35:10, 25; 36:1, 2, 8; 31:6, d0); "whom I have filled with a spirit of skill" (Exo 28:3) [X]; "every craftsman in whose mind [heart] the Lord had put skill, everyone whose heart stirred him up" (Exo 36:2); "whose hearts stirred them to use their skill" (Exo 35:26); [Claude reading] Wisdom in the heart includes craft skill. God puts it there, and the stirred heart puts it to work.

16069.text: Hardening | "I will harden [*strengthen*] his heart" (Exo 4:21); "Pharaoh's heart was hardened" (Exo 7:13, 22; 8:19; 9:12, 35; 10:20, 27; 11:10; 14:4, 8, 17); "to harden their hearts … that they should come against Israel" (Jos 11:20); "you shall not harden your heart or shut your hand against your poor brother" (Deu 15:7); Zedekiah "hardened his heart against turning to the Lord" (2Ch 36:13)

16274.text: Spirit: "I will put my Spirit within you, and you shall live" (Eze 37:14) [D1]; "when I pour out my Spirit upon the house of Israel" (Eze 39:29) [D1]; "formed the spirit of man within him" (Zec 12:1) [H1]; "he who is humble and contrite in spirit and trembles at my word" (Isa 66:2) [H1]; "every heart will melt … every spirit will faint" (Eze 21:7) [H2]

16330.text: 4.5 The servant's soul; the Son's life given in service: "Gladden the soul of your servant, for to you, O Lord, do I lift up my soul" (Psa 86:4); "destroy all the adversaries of my soul, for I am your servant" (Psa 143:12); "The Lord redeems the life of his servants" (Psa 34:22); "Preserve my life … save your servant" (Psa 86:2); "my servant … in whom my soul delights; I have put my Spirit upon him" (Isa 42:1); "the Son of Man came not to be served but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many" (Mar 10:45; Mat 20:28); "I do not account my life of any value … if only I may finish … the ministry" (Act 20:24); "risking his life … in your service" (Phili 2:30)

16364.text: The law in the heart: "the people in whose heart is my law" (Isa 51:7); "The law of his God is in his heart; his steps do not slip" (Psa 37:31); "I will put my law within them, and I will write it on their hearts" (Jer 31:33; Heb 8:10; 10:16)

16384.text: Written on the heart: Jer 31:33; Heb 8:10; 10:16. Kept in fear: "I will put the fear of me in their hearts, that they may not turn from me" (Jer 32:40).

16386.text: The Spirit and the covenant: "this is my covenant with them … My Spirit that is upon you, and my words that I have put in your mouth, shall not depart" (Isa 59:21) [D1]; "according to the covenant that I made with you … My Spirit remains in your midst" (Hag 2:5) [D1]; "a new covenant, not of the letter but of the Spirit. For the letter kills, but the Spirit gives life" (2Co 3:6); "profaned the blood of the covenant … and has outraged the Spirit of grace" (Heb 10:29)

16434.text: God's soul delights: "my chosen, in whom my soul delights [*is pleased*]" (Isa 42:1).

16455.text: 11.2 New heart, new spirit — renewal of the inner seat (M45): "I will give them one heart, and a new spirit I will put within them. I will remove the heart of stone from their flesh and give them a heart of flesh" (Eze 11:19; 36:26) [H1]

16459.text: 11.2 New heart, new spirit — renewal of the inner seat (M45): "my color changed, but I kept the matter in my heart" (Dan 7:28); [Claude reading] Renewal is predicated of heart and spirit together (Eze 11:19; 18:31; 36:26; Psa 51:10). Eze 18:31 makes it the person's task and Eze 36:26 makes it God's gift. Batch C §8.3 already noted the heart / spirit / flesh triad in these verses.

16481.text: Flesh first, then breath: "I will … cause flesh to come upon you, and cover you with skin, and put breath in you, and you shall live" (Eze 37:6); "flesh had come upon them, and skin had covered them. But there was no breath in them" (Eze 37:8). [Claude reading] Covered flesh without *rûaḥ* is not yet life. The two-stage sequence keeps flesh and breath distinct.

16488.text: Blessing and the heart's acts: "Blessed be the Lord … who put such a thing as this into the heart of the king" (Ezr 7:27); "My heart goes out to the commanders … Bless the Lord" (Judg 5:9); "your heart shall not be grudging … for this the Lord your God will bless you" (Deu 15:10); "if you will not take it to heart … I will curse your blessings" (Mal 2:2); "when all these things come upon you, the blessing and the curse … and you call them to mind [*bring them back to your heart*]" (Deu 30:1)

16514.text: The Spirit causes obedience: "I will put my Spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes and be careful to obey my rules" (Eze 36:27) [D1].

16516.text: The breastpiece of judgment on Aaron's heart: "Aaron shall bear the judgment of the people of Israel on his heart before the Lord regularly" (Exo 28:29–30). This is the literal chest, but it is the one place in the batch where the heart carries other people before God.

16517.text: Divine [D1]: "filled with power, with the Spirit of the Lord, and with justice and might, to declare to Jacob his transgression" (Mic 3:8); "I have put my Spirit upon him; he will bring forth justice" (Isa 42:1)

16637.text: Resisted or wronged: "you always resist the Holy Spirit" — "uncircumcised in heart" (Act 7:51); "lie to the Holy Spirit" (Act 5:3); "do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God" (Eph 4:30); blasphemy (Mar 3:29; Mat 12:32; Luk 12:10); OT: "they rebelled and grieved his Holy Spirit" (Isa 63:10); "take not your Holy Spirit from me" (Psa 51:11); "who put in the midst of them his Holy Spirit" (Isa 63:11)

16731.text: Hardened: "the Lord hardened the heart of Pharaoh king of Egypt" (Exo 14:8; 4:21); "the Lord your God hardened his spirit and made his heart obstinate, that he might give him into your hand" (Deu 2:30) [H1] (Sihon)

16830.text: 5.5 ◆ Fringe (M74): "guard the doors of your mouth from her who lies in your arms [*bosom*]" (Mic 7:5) — the closest intimacy as the place for guarding; The Gerasene: "He was kept under guard and bound with chains … but he would break the bonds and be driven by the demon" (Luk 8:29) [O] — human guarding fails against the spirit; the word of Jesus succeeds (8:29a); "who sit in tombs, and spend the night in secret places [*nāṣar*] … eat pig's flesh" (Isa 65:4); "they desire to have you circumcised that they may boast in your flesh" (Gal 6:13); "guard the good deposit … by the Holy Spirit who dwells within us" (2Ti 1:14) [D1]; "maintain the unity of the Spirit" (Eph 4:3) [D2]; "I will put my Spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes and be careful to obey" (Eze 36:27) [D1] — the carefulness is caused by the Spirit

17045.text: God's soul delights: "my chosen, in whom my soul delights; I have put my Spirit upon him" (Isa 42:1) [D1]; "my beloved with whom my soul is well pleased. I will put my Spirit upon him" (Mat 12:18) [D1]; "if he shrinks back, my soul has no pleasure in him" (Heb 10:38)

17061.text: God choosing with his soul and heart: "my chosen, in whom my soul delights; I have put my Spirit upon him" (Isa 42:1; Mat 12:18); "I have chosen and consecrated this house … My eyes and my heart will be there for all time" (2Ch 7:16); "God chose you … through sanctification by the Spirit" (2Th 2:13) [D2]

17073.text: Positive flesh-heart: "written … with the Spirit of the living God, not on tablets of stone but on tablets of human [*fleshly*] hearts" (2Co 3:3) [D1]. This echoes the "heart of flesh" of Eze 36:26 (§8.3).

17136.text: 8.3 God removes and replaces — heart, spirit and flesh in one act: "I will give them one heart, and a new spirit I will put within them. I will remove the heart of stone from their flesh and give them a heart of flesh" (Eze 11:19; 36:26) [H1]; "remove the foreskin of your hearts" (Jer 4:4)

17139.text: 8.3 God removes and replaces — heart, spirit and flesh in one act: [Claude reading] In Eze 11:19 / 36:26, heart, spirit and flesh are all tagged "remove" within four positions. Flesh is the good material here (a "heart of flesh") and stone is the bad, the reverse of NT flesh-desire (§1.11). Compare 2Co 3:3 (§3.3).

17234.text: b. The physical heart and the chest: Arrows and javelins pierce it (2Ki 9:24; 2Sa 18:14; Psa 45:5; 37:15).; God will "tear open their breast" (Hos 13:8).; Aaron bears the names of Israel and the Urim and Thummim *"on his heart"*, on the breastpiece (Exo 28:29–30).; fringe [Claude reading]: the physical place and the inner seat are one word. Aaron's breastpiece is a physical act of *carrying people on one's heart before the Lord*.

17237.text: e. Willing, deciding, purposing, being moved: *Deciding:*; "Daniel resolved" (Dan 1:8); "Joash decided" (2Ch 24:4); "has determined this in his heart" (1Co 7:37); "Each one must give as he has decided in his heart" (2Co 9:7); "of my own will / accord" (Num 24:13; 16:28, lēv); "It is in my heart to make a covenant" (2Ch 29:10); "I had it in my heart to build a house" (1Ch 22:7; 28:2; 1Ki 8:17–18); *Being moved to give:* "everyone whose heart stirred him … and everyone whose spirit moved him" (Exo 35:21); also Exo 25:2; 35:5, 22, 26, 29; 36:2; 2Ki 12:4 ("the money that a man's heart prompts him to bring").; *Intention as depth:* "The purpose in a man's heart is like deep water, but a man of understanding will draw it out" (Pro 20:5); "the inward mind and heart of a man are deep" (Psa 64:6).

17243.text: k. Heart states described through materials [Claude reading on the pattern; the images are the text's]: stone (Eze 11:19; 36:26; Job 41:24; 1Sa 25:37 "his heart died within him, and he became as a stone"); diamond (Zec 7:12); wax, water, melting (Psa 22:14; Jos 7:5; 2Sa 17:10); fat, unfeeling (Psa 119:70); "fattened your hearts" (Jam 5:5); oven (Hos 7:6); deep water (Pro 20:5); a stream of water in God's hand (Pro 21:1); grass struck down and withered (Psa 102:4); burning (Luk 24:32); a mirror: "As in water face reflects face, so the heart of man reflects the man" (Pro 27:19)

17273.text: 3.3 Unity and division: *Unity:*; "unite my heart" (Psa 86:11); "one heart" (Jer 32:39; Eze 11:19; 2Ch 30:12); "one heart and soul" (Act 4:32); "one spirit, with one mind" (Phili 1:27); "one flesh" (Gen 2:24); "he who is joined to the Lord becomes one spirit with him" (1Co 6:17); *Division:*; "double heart" (Psa 12:2); "double-minded" (Jam 4:8); "his heart was not wholly true" (1Ki 11:4; 15:3); "not with a whole heart" (2Ch 25:2); "The spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak" (Mat 26:41); "the desires of the flesh are against the Spirit … to keep you from doing the things you want to do" (Gal 5:17); [Claude reading] Division *within* a person is described as a split heart or as spirit against flesh. Union *between* persons uses the same terms (one heart, one soul, one flesh, one spirit).

17281.text: 3.10 God, animals and things — the vocabulary is not limited to humans ◆ fringe: *God has a heart:* grieved (Gen 6:6); speaks in it (Gen 8:21); "a man after my own heart" (1Sa 13:14; Act 13:22); "My heart recoils within me; my compassion grows warm and tender" (Hos 11:8); "he does not afflict from his heart" (Lam 3:33); "my eyes and my heart will be there" (1Ki 9:3); "the intents of his heart" (Jer 23:20); "with all my heart and all my soul" (Jer 32:41).; *God has a soul:* "my soul hates" (Isa 1:14); "my soul delights" (Isa 42:1; Mat 12:18); "my soul shall not abhor you" (Lev 26:11); "Does your soul loathe Zion?" (Jer 14:19); "my soul has no pleasure in him" (Heb 10:38); "The Lord God has sworn by himself [nephesh]" (Amo 6:8; Jer 51:14); "shall I not avenge myself [nephesh]" (Jer 5:9, 29; 9:9).; *God's spirit and breath:* "the breath of his mouth" (Psa 33:6); "the breath of his lips" (Isa 11:4); "God is spirit" (Joh 4:24).; *Animals:*; "living creatures" (nephesh, Gen 1); "They all have the same breath" (Ecc 3:19); "the spirit of the beast" (Ecc 3:21); a beast's mind given to a man (Dan 4:16); "the spirit of the living creatures was in the wheels" (Eze 1:20–21; 10:17); "all flesh" includes animals (Gen 6–9); *Places and things:* heart of the sea, earth and heaven (§2.1a); Sheol's appetite (Isa 5:14); idols with no breath (§2.3e).

17460.text: The prophet's own delight. *"I am about to take the delight of your eyes away from you at a stroke; yet you shall not mourn or weep … So I spoke to the people in the morning, and at evening my wife died"* (Eze 24:16–18). The verses already in 10.6 (24:21, 25) explain the sign to the people. Here it is first a man's wife.

18513.text: Most add nothing new: the priestly "lest you die" statutes (Exo 28–30, Lev 8–22, Num 1–18: 21 verses); the trial and condemnation verses of Jesus (Mat 20:18; 26:66; Mar 10:33; 14:64; 15:44; Luk 23:15, 22; 24:20; Joh 18:14, 32; 19:7; Act 13:28); burial instructions and notices of approaching death (Gen 47:29; 50:5, 16; 1Ki 2:1); danger and sickness verses already carried by a parallel (2Ki 20:1 = Isa 38:1; Luk 8:42; Joh 4:47, 49); These are left as data. The verses below carry something the narrative does not.

18935.text: Books: Isaiah is high because of H8213 "bring low" (Isa 2, 5, 25, 26) and the Sennacherib account (Isa 37). Mark is the mute spirit and the silencing words.

19698.text: Narrative: 10 verses are cited.; Deu 30:19 in Ch 2 and 10.7; Job 7:15 and Jer 8:3 in Ch 2 ("Wanting to die"); Pro 1:29 in 10.2; Isa 66:4 in 10.12; Act 10:41 in Ch 2; new in v2: Psa 106:23 in 10.13 ("Pleading, and standing in the breach"); Isa 42:1 in Ch 9; Luk 10:42 in 10.1 ("What anxiety does"); Phili 1:22 in Ch 7; The other 222 are uncited. 10.7 *Choosing and setting direction* carries only Deu 30:19 from these words.

19726.text: The servant: "Behold my servant, whom I uphold, my chosen, in whom my soul delights; I have put my Spirit upon him" (Isa 42:1). Mat 12:18 carries the same words with G0140: "my servant whom I have chosen, my beloved with whom my soul is well pleased. I will put my Spirit upon him".

19764.text: Isa 42:1 | soul (God's), Spirit | "my chosen, in whom my soul delights; I have put my Spirit upon him"

19913.text: Isa 42:1 | 13.1 v9 *Choosing*, through Mat 12:18 "quoting Isaiah 42:1", with the servant's bearing (Mat 12:19–20 = Isa 42:2–3) | You ruled that Mat 12:18 points to Jesus, part of the divine. So the servant's quiet and gentle bearing belongs to 13.1, where it already stands. I recommend no 10.7 *Being chosen* placement.

19924.text: 3.6 Exo 36:2, in 10.7 *Willing*, *The willing heart*: Add a bullet after the Exo 35:21–22 bullet: > - Of the craftsmen, the skill given and the heart that moves are named together: *"every craftsman in whose mind the Lord had put skill, everyone whose heart stirred him up to come to do the work"* (Exodus 36:2).

20118.text: The will steers. *"they are guided by a very small rudder wherever the will of the pilot directs"* (Jam 3:4). The will is pictured as what sets a ship's direction. In its passage (3:3–5) the picture is used of the tongue.

20183.text: The pilot's will. *"they are guided by a very small rudder wherever the will of the pilot directs"* (Jam 3:4). In its passage the picture belongs to the tongue: *"we guide their whole bodies"* (3:3), *"So also the tongue is a small member"* (3:5). The will directs a whole ship; the tongue sets on fire *"the entire course of life"* (3:6).

20333.text: Isa 42:1 | ✅ Accurate | Include: new | M39 God's delight (13.1); M24 in the passage

20403.text: Isa 42:1 | God has a soul (Ch 9, 11) | no | God's choosing with delight and Spirit (13.1); the chosen one's bearing (10.7)

20433.text: The other 17 have something the narrative does not carry for M64. ~~In 6 of them the narrative never quotes the M64 word at all: Isa 42:1, Luk 10:42, Phili 1:22, Deu 2:30, Psa 32:2 and Isa 10:7.~~ *(v2: in 4 of them the narrative never quotes the M64 word: Isa 42:1, Luk 10:42, Phili 1:22 and Deu 2:30. Isa 10:7 is quoted in 10.13, and Psa 32:2's counting through Rom 4:8 in 10.9.)*

20474.text: Written on by God: Hebrews 8:10 and 10:16, where the pairing of "hearts" and "minds" is reversed between the two verses.

20494.text: 2. Inward: outside influences → heart and mind.: God writes on minds and hearts (Heb 8:10; 10:16) and fills people with skill (Exod 35:35).; Instruction gives discretion (Prov 1:4).; Counsel establishes plans (Prov 15:22; 20:18).; The serpent leads thoughts astray (2 Cor 11:3), and "the god of this world" blinds (2 Cor 4:4).

20509.text: The source is shaped from outside: God writes on minds (Heb 8:10); minds blinded (2Co 4:4) (§9.1.4): Ch 11 §1 "The inner being is acted upon as much as it acts"

20566.text: *dianoia* | The mind given wholly to love God · the mind hostile · the mind darkened because of hardness of heart · the mind's desires, "children of wrath" · proud in the thoughts of their hearts · laws written on minds · minds prepared · a sincere mind stirred · understanding given | Mat 22:37; Mar 12:30; Luk 10:27 · Col 1:21 · Eph 4:18 · Eph 2:3 · Luk 1:51 · Heb 8:10; 10:16 · 1Pe 1:13 · 2Pe 3:1 · 1Jo 5:20 | Eph 4:18 states the causal direction: "darkened in their understanding … due to their hardness of heart." The heart's state changes the mind's character (S). Eph 2:3 links the mind's desires to wrath (anger strand)

20816.text: The verb puts a question to a person for information (tree H7592 1a1 'to ask, ask for', 1a3 'to enquire, enquire of').

20817.text: The asking is a pursuit: he seeks to learn something from her.

20818.text: What he asks is whose daughter she is, her family.

20819.text: The servant asks; Rebekah is the one asked and she answers him.

20820.text: The servant is telling how it went at the spring, after she had given him and his camels drink (Gen 24:45-46).

20821.text: The servant asked Rebekah to name her family.

20822.text: He asked, she named her father and grandfather, and then he gave her the ring and bracelets.

20823.text: He asks to learn whether she belongs to his master's kin.

20824.text: Discovery: the purpose behind the question is read from verse 48; the passage is needed to settle it.

20940.text: The verb is asking for something as a favour (tree H7592 1a2 'to ask (as a favour), borrow'), here asking neighbours for goods.

20941.text: The asking is a pursuit: each woman is to seek goods from her neighbour.

20942.text: What is asked for is silver and gold articles and clothing.

20943.text: The asking ends in plunder: the Egyptians are stripped of these things.

20944.text: Each Israelite woman asks; her neighbour and the Egyptians are the ones asked.

20945.text: These are God's words of what will happen when the people go out of Egypt (Exo 3:20-21).

20946.text: Each woman is told to ask her neighbour and the woman in her house for goods.

20947.text: They ask, they put what they receive on their sons and daughters, and so they plunder the Egyptians.

20948.text: The favour God gives the people in the sight of the Egyptians is what the asking draws on.

20949.text: Discovery: what the asking amounts to, a request granted or a borrowing, the claims process tests against the other verses of this asking.

21279.text: Aloud, negated, gives withheld voice: the sigh of grief is to be kept inward and not voiced.

21308.text: Call is here the judgement a person puts on a thing in naming it (calling evil good, the Sabbath a delight, a fast acceptable): a valuing of the heart voiced in speech.

21346.text: Deal is here the outward act of dealing with a person, with a disposition (kindness, loyalty, honesty, courage or good faith) named by another word of the verse; it bears on the one dealt with and names no inner operation of its own.

21383.text: New gives newness to the heart or spirit: a changed condition of the seat of the person, which the verse sets against the heart of stone or against transgression.

21393.text: Old is here the former time (the days of old, the things of old) as what remembering, considering or comfort is directed at; the inner act is named by another word of the verse.

21456.text: Holiness here is the holiness or sacredness of a place, day, offering, oil, writing or thing set apart (a holy place, a sacred gift, the holy mountain); no inner-being operation is voiced by it.

how_to_fill: evaluations: one for each surface item (vl_id); observations: one for each surface and role; existing: an action for each existing observation (accept, modify, delete, merge, leave). See USER-GUIDE section 8.18.
